_comment: Outreach sequence template library. Each sequence defines touches with timing offsets. dayOffset is calendar days after the previous touch (0 = same day as sequence start). These drive the scheduled-draft engine: all touches are pre-written as Gmail drafts when the user starts a sequence; each step surface in the stale engine when its dayOffset has elapsed.

sequences.label: Cold intro to hiring principal
sequences.scenario: You have identified the VP/Director who leads the target function — the person you would likely report to. You want to introduce yourself with a concrete proof point and request a brief connection.

touches.label: Cold intro
touches.tone: Direct, senior peer. Lead with one concrete proof point (the artifact link). Under 80 words. Low-friction ask: a 15-min intro call.

touches.label: Follow-up
touches.tone: Add genuine new value — a relevant market observation or a specific question about their function. Do not re-pitch. Under 60 words.

touches.label: Final ping
touches.tone: Graceful last touch. Acknowledge this is the final note. Leave the door open with no pressure. Under 40 words.

sequences.label: Cold intro to the CRO
sequences.scenario: You have identified the CRO. You want to open with a useful point of view about pipeline coverage and forecast accuracy, grounded in one specific observation about their revenue engine.

touches.label: Cold intro
touches.tone: Lead with a point of view about where their pipeline number comes from and whether the forecast can be trusted. Reference one concrete observation or artifact, never a list. Do not lead with your availability or ask to chat about the role. Under 90 words. End with one low-friction question.

touches.label: Follow-up
touches.tone: Add one new concrete observation or artifact about pipeline coverage or forecast confidence. Do not repeat the opener or stack examples. Ask one useful question. Under 60 words.

touches.label: Final ping
touches.tone: Graceful last touch. Acknowledge this is the final note. Leave the door open with no pressure. Under 40 words.

sequences.label: Cold intro to the CFO
sequences.scenario: You have identified the CFO. You want to open with a useful point of view about acquisition cost and comp-plan leakage, grounded in one specific observation about their revenue economics.

touches.label: Cold intro
touches.tone: Lead with a point of view about what they spend to acquire revenue or where incentives may leak money without producing the intended behavior. Reference one concrete observation or artifact, never a list. Do not lead with your availability or ask to chat about the role. Under 90 words. End with one low-friction question.

touches.label: Follow-up
touches.tone: Add one new concrete observation or artifact about acquisition cost or comp-plan leakage. Do not repeat the opener or stack examples. Ask one financially grounded question. Under 60 words.

sequences.label: Cold intro to the VP of Sales
sequences.scenario: You have identified the VP of Sales. You want to open with a useful point of view about rep productivity and ramp time, grounded in one specific observation about how the sales team operates.

touches.label: Cold intro
touches.tone: Lead with a point of view about what reps spend their day on or how long new reps take to carry quota. Reference one concrete observation or artifact, never a list. Do not lead with your availability or ask to chat about the role. Under 90 words. End with one low-friction question.

touches.label: Follow-up
touches.tone: Add one new concrete observation or artifact about rep productivity or ramp time. Do not repeat the opener or stack examples. Ask one practical sales question. Under 60 words.

touches.label: Final ping
touches.tone: Graceful last touch. Acknowledge this is the final note. Leave the door open with no pressure. Under 40 words.

sequences.label: Cold intro to the demand generation lead
sequences.scenario: You have identified the demand generation lead. You want to open with a useful point of view about lead quality, follow-up speed and the handoff from marketing to sales development, grounded in one specific observation.

touches.label: Cold intro
touches.tone: Lead with a point of view about lead quality or the friction between marketing and sales development over the handoff and follow-up speed. Reference one concrete observation or artifact, never a list. Do not lead with your availability or ask to chat about the role. Under 90 words. End with one low-friction question.

touches.label: Follow-up
touches.tone: Add one new concrete observation or artifact about lead quality, follow-up speed or the sales handoff. Do not repeat the opener or stack examples. Ask one useful question. Under 60 words.

sequences.label: Cold intro to TA/recruiter (gatekeeper)
sequences.scenario: You have a TA or recruiter contact at a company you have applied to. You want help with process, timeline and logistics only, without treating them as the hiring decision-maker or pitching revenue strategy.

touches.label: Intro + confirm
touches.tone: Brief, professional and limited to process. Mention the specific role, ask whether the application was received, and clarify the timeline or next logistical step. Do not pitch revenue strategy or ask them to judge fit. Under 60 words.

touches.label: Follow-up
touches.tone: Short process check-in. Ask about timing, status or one necessary logistical detail. Do not add a strategic pitch or press for a hiring decision. Under 50 words.

sequences.label: LinkedIn connection request to hiring principal
sequences.scenario: You want to connect with a hiring principal on LinkedIn. The note must be under 300 characters.

touches.label: Connection note
touches.tone: Under 300 characters. One sentence on shared domain expertise. One sentence on the specific reason you're reaching out. Sign off with first name only. NO em dashes.

sequences.label: LinkedIn connection request to TA/recruiter
sequences.scenario: You want to connect with a TA or recruiter on LinkedIn who is at a company you have applied to.

touches.label: Connection note
touches.tone: Under 300 characters. Mention the specific role you applied to. Ask if they are the right person for that search. Sign off with first name only. NO em dashes.

sequences.label: Post-application warm follow-up (applied, no contact yet)
sequences.scenario: You have applied to a role but have no specific contact. This sequence surfaces in the stale engine as a nudge to find a contact, then provides a template once one is found.

touches.label: First follow-up
touches.tone: Brief, professional. Reference the specific role. One concrete proof point. Low-friction ask: confirm the application is under review. Under 70 words.

touches.label: Second follow-up
touches.tone: Short. Add one new insight or recent proof point. Acknowledge this is a follow-up. Under 50 words.
